Index: Panel A. IRRs are per 10-percentile increase in the index. Unless noted, models are negative binomial (NB2) with the dispersion (alpha) estimated by maximum likelihood and an offset of log(adults aged ≥45 years). The primary analysis is the SVI and EDI model adjusted for metropolitan status. Second term: metropolitan status (RUCC 1-3 vs 4-9), ordinal RUCC per 1-code increase, or log population density per 1-unit increase.

Panel A has 76 rows from 72 fitted models: the three SVI quartile contrasts for each outcome come from one model. Weighting: the NB2 model weights each county's rate by N/(1 + alpha x mu), which rises with population (N) and levels off. Population-weighted rows are Poisson regressions with the same offset, which weight each county's rate by its adults aged ≥45 years and so describe the average adult; rows with counties weighted equally use weights 1/N and describe the average county; both have robust (HC0) standard errors. Under population weights the Kish effective sample size is 314 of 3,144 counties, and the largest 1% of counties carry 22.3% of the weight.

Stratified rows marked Poisson: the NB2 dispersion estimate lay on its boundary (alpha = 0), the information matrix could not be inverted at the optimizer's stopping point, and the Poisson log-likelihood was at least as high, so the maximum-likelihood NB2 fit is the Poisson fit, shown here with a profile-likelihood interval. For cardiac MR each of the 14 nonmetropolitan facilities is in a different county; for cardiac CT the 115 nonmetropolitan facilities are in 108 counties (seven with two), and the counts show no overdispersion (see Supplementary Table S4 and Supplementary Methods S4). Facility totals differ by index because counties without an index value are excluded.

Panel B covers the unadjusted and metropolitan-adjusted SVI, EDI and SDI models (12 index-outcome models, each fitted as Poisson, NB2 with dispersion estimated, and NB2 with dispersion fixed at 1); it does not cover the other Panel A sensitivity rows.

CCT = cardiac computed tomography; CI = confidence interval; CMR = cardiac magnetic resonance; EDI = economic deprivation index; IRR = incidence rate ratio; NB2 = negative binomial (quadratic variance); NE = not estimable; RUCC = Rural-Urban Continuum Code; SDI = Social Deprivation Index; SVI = Social Vulnerability Index.
